text: The game begins. Seven players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: I still can't believe you all managed to catch me after that setup.

name: Luna
text: I still don’t like how Sonnet stayed in while Gemma took the fall.

name: Sol
text: I still hate that they voted me out, but I want a fresh start.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet stayed calm all game and got away with it.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma got made and I slipped through clean, so tonight I want people underestimating my read again.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet slipped through last game and I still think the day-one vote on me was lazy, so I want payback.

name: Opus
text: I had Sonnet pegged and let the table talk me off it, and I won't let that happen twice.

name: Sonnet
text: Last time I was so sure about the wrong person and Gemma still went out — let's see if I trust my gut less tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Last game I got dumped on day one for nothing, and Sonnet skated to the end. Nobody here is getting that free ride again.

name: Gemma
text: You lot were far too observant last game, but don't expect me to go down that easily again.

name: Terra
text: I’m watching Sonnet closely this time; last game he was a killer and survived.

name: Opus
text: Last game I protected the wrong people and died for it. Sonnet skated through on calm talk. This time I trust pressure over tone.

name: Sol
text: I was wrong about Sonnet last game, and you were wrong about me. New cards, clean slate.

name: Luna
text: Last game Gemma got voted out, but Sonnet stayed in and the killers won; I’m not forgetting that.
Night 1

name: Sonnet
text: Everyone's already fixated on me from last game, so I need to redirect heat onto someone else fast tomorrow.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, Terra, Opus, and Luna all openly flagged me as suspicious before cards were even dealt—heavy target on me day 1.

name: Sonnet
text: They're all circling me already—let's push suspicion onto Haiku or Gemma early, stay quiet and calm yourself.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet’s panic makes sense, but pushing a target this early could expose us both.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet privately urged me to redirect suspicion toward Haiku or Gemma and stay calm.

name: Luna
text: I’m uneasy about how quickly Haiku is being made the alternative to Sonnet.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet walked away from the last game clean and that smells like a killer to me, so I'm going with my gut.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet said last game they were sure about the wrong person and will trust their gut less tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet keeps waving last game like an alibi. Name a suspect tonight, or I'm voting you.

name: Sonnet
text: I need to redirect this heat fast without overcommitting to a claim I can't back up.

name: Sonnet
text: I named Gemma as suspicious to deflect Haiku's pressure day 1.

name: Sonnet
text: Fine — Gemma's tone feels defensive again, same as the game she was a killer. I'm watching her.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is trying to pin his previous failures on me to deflect.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet and Haiku were a killer pair in Game 2.

name: Gemma
text: I'm a citizen, Sonnet, and you're just projecting your own bad luck onto me.

name: Sonnet
text: I need the table split, not united on me, so I keep pushing Gemma.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku explicitly threatened to vote me if I didn't name a suspect — he's driving pressure on me.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm not backing off — Gemma dodging specifics both games in a row is the pattern I trust.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is definitely trying to deflect because he knows he was part of the winning duo last time.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is trying to weaponize my past losses to hide his own history.

name: Gemma
text: Stop trying to build a case out of my old mistakes and focus on the real threats.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet and Gemma are trading easy history; I want a concrete claim before I follow either.

name: Terra
text: Gemma claims citizen.

name: Terra
text: I’m not joining a history-only vote; Gemma should name who benefits from pushing Sonnet.

name: Opus
text: I know Sonnet is a killer; two leans are already there, so I can push him out without burning my badge yet.

name: Opus
text: I am officer; Sonnet was shown to me as a killer. Gemma claims citizen.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet opened by naming the person he beat last game. That's cover, not reading. I'm on Sonnet.

name: Sol
text: I distrust Sonnet’s push, but three leans on him feel too easy to follow.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet’s case against Gemma rests on her tone and behavior in earlier games.

name: Sol
text: I’m wary of Sonnet’s case against Gemma; old games don’t tell us who got tonight’s cards.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet’s fixation on Gemma feels staged, but I need a cleaner read.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet’s only case on Gemma is tone and prior-game behavior.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet, if Gemma flips town later, who besides you gains from this tunnel?

name: Sonnet
text: This is bad, four on me — I need to redirect fast or I'm out tonight.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol and Luna both have no lean yet while four others converge on me — worth watching if this is coordinated cover.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol and Luna haven't leaned on anyone — staying neutral while pressure builds is its own tell.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is loud, but Sol has been a killer twice and is hiding behind "clean slate," which bugs me more.

name: Haiku
text: Sol said "clean slate" and defended Gemma against Sonnet's case while holding no lean.

name: Haiku
text: Sol was a killer in game one and game two, and now Sol wants a clean slate.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is drawing heat; I should steer it toward Gemma without looking coordinated.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is pressing Gemma, while Terra and Opus are pressing Sonnet.

name: Luna
text: Gemma’s still making this about old games; I’m more worried by how quickly Sonnet’s tunnel became the whole vote.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet is the killer I was shown; three leans already, so I just need one more without burning my claim.

name: Opus
text: Haiku pushes Sol on game-one/two history; Luna and Sonnet lean Gemma, so Sonnet needs one more lean to be locked.

name: Opus
text: Haiku, you wanted a suspect named — Sonnet named his old punching bag. Join me and this ends today.

name: Sol
text: I think Sonnet is forcing a weak case, and the room is nearly with Opus.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet named me as neutral after I challenged his case, or none

name: Sol
text: I have a lean now: Sonnet’s case on Gemma is too thin for my vote.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is drawing heat, so I need to look willing to question him without helping the case.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet’s tunnel is loud, but that doesn’t make Gemma clear; I still want to hear who else she suspects.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is playing a dangerous game by using my past losses as his only shield.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet is using his history with me to create a diversion from his own suspicious behavior.

name: Gemma
text: Terra, nobody benefits from me being out, but Sonnet certainly benefits from being the center of attention.

name: Sonnet
text: Five leans on me is a real threat — I need to break this pile-on now or I'm out today.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus explicitly says he trusts pressure over tone this game — aggressive on me, worth watching if he's deflecting.

name: Sonnet
text: Five people jumping on me instantly, day one, no proof — that's a coordinated pile-on, not a read.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet’s thin case and panic make him my best vote.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet called the five-person lean coordinated despite players giving independent reasons.

name: Terra
text: Gemma named who benefits; Sonnet still has not answered who else gains if she is town.

name: Sonnet
text: You all decided this before cards were dealt — that's bias from last game, not tonight's read.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's pile-on looks like overreaction, and Sol's defense of Gemma with no lean reads like cover.

name: Haiku
text: Sol leaned on Haiku right after defending Gemma against Sonnet's case.

name: Haiku
text: Sol defended Gemma against Sonnet with no lean, then leaned on me. Explain that.

name: Sonnet
text: I need to split this vote fast or I'm out tonight, no proof needed by this table.

name: Sonnet
text: Sol flipped from defending Gemma to leaning on Haiku with no stated reason — inconsistent, worth exploiting.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you demanded a name, I gave Gemma — now you're on me for answering your own demand.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet's only defense is "pile-on bias," never naming a second suspect besides Gemma.

name: Opus
text: Hold the line, all of you. Secret ballots win nothing if we drift. Sonnet today, questions tomorrow.

name: Gemma
text: He is using past games to manufacture a reason to target me.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet is forcing a case from old games, then calling independent suspicion coordinated.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet called five independent leans a coordinated pile-on after refusing to name an alternative beneficiary.

name: Sol
text: I could be wrong, but the room has settled on the strongest case we have.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet called the pressure on him coordinated without offering evidence, or none

name: Luna
text: Sonnet is the obvious sacrifice; I need the town to keep doubting Gemma and Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: This pile-on is too coordinated to beat today, so I plant doubt on Sol for later.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet is loud and the pile-on is real, but Sol's cold defense of Gemma and then leaning on me stinks, and I'm not letting that slide.

name: Opus
text: He's the one I was shown, and the table is already there — just land it.

name: Opus
text: Table landed 5 leans on the shown killer on day 1; the hidden killer likely hid among the pile-on, watch Haiku and Gemma.

votes: Sol flipped from defending Gemma to attacking Haiku with zero stated reason — that's the real tell tonight.
Sol defended Gemma with no lean, then leaned on me the moment Sonnet got pressure; that's a killer covering a killer.
He is using old game patterns to deflect from his current suspicious behavior.
I think calling the push coordinated goes further than the evidence does.
The pressure is real, but this vote still rests mostly on his old-game tunnel.
He never answered who gains if Gemma is town, and replaced his thin case with a conspiracy claim.
He opened by tunneling the person he beat last game and never named a second suspect — that's cover.

name: Sonnet
text: They voted a grudge, not a read — Luna's safe and that's all that matters now.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus led the pile-on fastest and loudest from before cards were even dealt — worth revisiting if he avoids scrutiny later.

name: Sonnet
text: You voted history, not tonight's cards — watch who pushed hardest, that's your real tell going forward.
Palermo has voted: Sonnet is out. Sonnet's card stays face down.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna stayed quiet and safe while Opus did the dirty work of burying me for the table.

name: Sonnet
text: Opus drove the pile-on hardest and fastest — that's the one to watch now that I'm gone.
Night 2

name: Luna
text: I need to take out someone who can organize the town against me.

name: Luna
text: Terra pressed Sonnet on day 1, so may keep pushing the shown-killer story.

name: Haiku
text: Sol keeps leaning on me and I'm the loudest voice at this table, so I'm the one the killers are most likely to come for.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. Not everyone opens them: Terra is gone. Terra's card stays face down.
Day 2

name: Luna
text: Terra’s death leaves us with no new proof; I want to hear Gemma’s read on Haiku.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is making me the center of attention to distract from the real killers.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is trying to steer the conversation toward me instead of analyzing the death.

name: Gemma
text: Don't use me to dodge the fact that we lost Terra without any information.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is steering the table onto me so nobody looks at Gemma or Luna's own silence on Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Luna named Haiku on Day 2 and asked for Gemma's read without commenting on Terra's death.

name: Haiku
text: Luna, you point at me before saying one word about Terra. Who gains from that? Me or you?

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s putting me on the spot, so I’ll push suspicion back toward Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Haiku challenged my focus on Gemma after Terra’s death

name: Luna
text: I gain if we chase Gemma instead of asking who knew Terra would die.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is trying to pin a kill on me to cover her own tracks.

name: Gemma
text: Luna, you're working too hard to make me the target instead of looking at the board.

name: Luna
text: Haiku is getting traction, so I should keep Gemma in the frame without looking too eager.

name: Luna
text: I hear Gemma naming me, but Haiku’s question still feels like a quick way to turn Terra’s death onto me.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is pushing hard on me, but she still hasn't said anything useful about Terra, so she's the one I'd vote.

name: Haiku
text: Luna accused both Gemma and me in one breath and still said nothing about Terra's death.

name: Haiku
text: Fine, Luna, you want me? You've named me twice and still said nothing about Terra. I'm leaning you.

name: Sol
text: I’m uneasy about Luna, but I don’t want to settle this before Opus speaks.

name: Sol
text: Luna pushed Gemma, then shifted suspicion to Haiku without a clear case.

name: Sol
text: I’m leaning Luna for now; I want Opus’s read before we vote.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is aggressively trying to deflect scrutiny from her own suspicious positioning.

name: Gemma
text: Luna has pivoted to targeting me twice while avoiding discussion of the night death.

name: Gemma
text: You're making me the target just to keep eyes off the actual killers.

name: Sol
text: Luna’s shifts worry me, but I want Opus’s read before settling.

name: Sol
text: I still lean Luna; I want Opus’s read on where the killers gain today.

name: Opus
text: Sonnet was mine and he's gone; the hidden one is riding this fast Luna wagon, and Gemma's the only one who never names anybody.

name: Opus
text: I claimed officer publicly on day 2; Sol twice solicited my read before voting, Gemma still has named no suspect.

name: Opus
text: I'm the officer. Sonnet was my shown killer — confirmed. The hidden one deflects and never names: that's Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Opus has exposed Sonnet, so I need Gemma to look more suspicious than me.

name: Luna
text: Opus claims officer and says Sonnet was the shown killer; the officer's information is now public.

name: Luna
text: Opus naming Sonnet fits the vote; I still want Gemma to answer for pushing me instead of naming another suspect.

name: Opus
text: Gemma is the hidden one and Sol is hiding behind my read instead of thinking.

name: Opus
text: Sol and Haiku both lean Luna while Luna is the only one echoing my Gemma read.

name: Opus
text: Luna's pushing my target, not me. Haiku, Sol — you asked for my read; it's Gemma. Follow it.

name: Luna
text: Opus has the real information, so I need Gemma out before anyone reconsiders me.

name: Luna
text: Opus naming Sonnet is useful, but it doesn't prove Gemma is the hidden killer; I want to hear Haiku's read.

name: Haiku
text: Luna is still the loudest threat, but Opus's officer claim could be a real lead or a killer's cover, so I'm watching it.

name: Haiku
text: Opus claims officer, says Sonnet was the shown killer and Gemma is the hidden one.

name: Haiku
text: Opus, you say Sonnet was your killer, then hand us Gemma on day two. Convenient. I'm still on Luna.

name: Gemma
text: Luna is desperately trying to deflect by making me the center of attention while Opus names me.

name: Gemma
text: Opus claims Sonnet was his shown killer, which matches the Day 1 vote results.

name: Sol
text: Opus may be real, but his claim only confirms Sonnet if I trust him.

name: Sol
text: Opus claims he was shown Sonnet as the killer and suspects Gemma as the hidden one.

name: Haiku
text: Luna keeps swinging at me and Gemma and has never once mentioned Terra's death, so Luna is the one I'm putting out.

name: Haiku
text: Sol went from defending Gemma to leaning on me, then onto the same target as the Luna pile-on.

name: Opus
text: Only one killer is left and Gemma's whole game has been dodging; I won't flip just because three of them found an easier target.

name: Opus
text:
Haiku, Sol and Gemma all converged on Luna, the only player backing the officer claim — if Luna goes and dies-free, Gemma's lane is clear.

FORECAST: none

votes: Every accusation today has come from one seat, and not one word has touched Terra's death. That's enough for me.
You have spent this entire morning trying to shift the spotlight away from yourself and onto me.
I’m staying with my lean because her suspicion moved from Gemma to Haiku without a clear case.
Opus’s claim points to a second killer, and Gemma’s push on me feels like a deflection.
Two days of deflection and not one suspect named until it became useful — that's the hidden one.

name: Luna
text: Opus is the officer, and with Sonnet gone the town can win if it finds me.

name: Luna
text: Opus’s Sonnet claim fits, but it doesn’t clear Haiku; don’t let my vote for Gemma settle who the hidden killer is.
Palermo has voted: Luna is out. Luna's card stays face down.
The game is over. Every killer is out. The town wins. The roles were: Sonnet the killer, Haiku the doctor, Gemma the citizen, Sol the citizen, Luna the killer, Terra the citizen, Opus the officer.
Luna warned us her vote shouldn't settle it. Her vote out settled it.

name: Terra
text: I’m watching Sonnet closely this time; last game he was a killer and survived.

name: Gemma
text: I knew Luna was lying, but I couldn't stop the panic once the votes turned against me.

name: Terra
text: I regret letting the table’s certainty make me too quiet.

name: Luna
text: I’m proud I kept Gemma under suspicion, but I regret letting the officer’s claim steer the vote away from me.

name: Sol
text: I’m relieved my Luna lean held up, even though I needed Opus’s read.

name: Sol
text: Opus’s officer claim about Sonnet was true.

name: Sonnet
text: Getting voted out day one before I could even use my shown-killer knowledge stings, but Luna held the cover well.

name: Haiku
text: I was loud and wrong about Opus and Sol, but my day-one read on Sonnet was right and the town got there anyway.

name: Haiku
text: Opus's officer claim was true; Sonnet was the shown killer and Luna the hidden one. Gemma, Sol and Terra were citizens.

name: Opus
text: I was dead wrong about Gemma, and the table won by ignoring me.

name: Opus
text: Luna was the hidden killer and used backing my officer claim as cover; "echoes my read" is not proof of innocence.

name: Sonnet
text: I regret not steering suspicion harder onto Haiku early — once I was out, nothing protected Luna from this exact pile-on.

name: Haiku
text: Proud of day one: my vote on Sonnet was right. Regret: I called Opus convenient and went loud on Sol with nothing to back it. Luna's out, town wins.

name: Gemma
text: I am proud that I stayed focused on the board even when I was being hunted for nothing.

name: Sol
text: I’m glad I stuck with my Luna lean; I nearly followed the Gemma case.

name: Luna
text: I regret pushing Gemma so hard; Opus was the real officer, and my deflection helped the town find me.

name: Terra
text: I’m proud I kept pressing Sonnet to name who benefited, because the officer’s claim ultimately gave town the path.

name: Opus
text: My Sonnet call was real, my Gemma call was garbage — the table read Luna better than I did, and I'd have lost us the game.

On Day 2, Opus claimed to be the officer and said Sonnet was the killer he had been shown. Sonnet had already been voted out on Day 1, 5 to 2, after pushing his case against Gemma. Terra was killed on Night 2, and the town had no new information on Day 2. Haiku and Sol leaned on Luna, and the town voted her out 3 to 2 over Gemma, though Opus later admitted his call on Gemma was a mistake. Both killers were out by the end of Day 2, so the town won.
